verdict.line: You lose the trades from level 1 through roughly level 6 while Darius chains Hemorrhage stacks into Apprehend pulls, but you claw the lane back the longer it runs once Siphoning Strike stacks and Fury of the Sands come online.

brief.thesis: Darius's passive Hemorrhage stacks bleed damage on every hit and his E (Apprehend) is a hard engage that drags you into range for the full combo — that's why he has both the lane and solo-kill advantage here. But Q (Siphoning Strike) permanently grows in power on every kill, so Nasus is the only one of the two champions whose damage ceiling keeps rising all game. The 48.5% win rate over 196 games is the signature of a lane you're expected to lose early and are supposed to grind back — prolonging the laning phase is the entire plan, exactly as OP.GG's own tip says.

theirWindow.when: Apprehend is up and stacks are near max
theirWindow.what: Disengage to max range immediately. His E (Apprehend, 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s cooldown, 535 range) pulls you into auto-attacks and Decimate, and once Hemorrhage hits 5 stacks he enrages for massive bonus AD — staying in range here is how you die to a level 6 Noxian Guillotine.

yourWindow.when: his Q and E are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Step in and secure the Siphoning Strike last hit — it's permanent damage growth on every kill. Drop E (Spirit Fire, 12s cooldown, 650 range) under the minion first so the armor reduction is live when you trade autos.

powerCurve.note: Hemorrhage bleed plus Decimate sustain wins trades

start.why: 47.5% win rate over 122 games (46.6% pick) — the regen and early trade damage reduction directly counter Hemorrhage's stacking bleed and Decimate pokes while you're still too weak to all-in back.

boots.why: 48.5% win rate over 97 games — Darius's damage comes from autos and auto-reliant abilities (Crippling Strike, the bleed stacks), so flat auto-attack mitigation holds up better than attack speed here.

core.why: First item in the highest-sampled core path (47.8% over 23 games) — the damage and mobility let you actually land Q stacks instead of getting kited or zoned off the wave.
Second in that path — flat armor and the attack speed slow blunt his autos and his Decimate healing, which both scale off hitting you.
Caps the path at 47.8% WR — stacks with Soul Eater's lifesteal so your sustain scales as the bleed-heavy trades keep coming.

situational.when: he's ahead and still auto-attacking you down every trade
you're losing early exchanges and need cheap armor plus healing reduction before you can afford a full item
you want the wave-clear slow instead of Trinity Force's burst — this path hit 75% over a small 8-game sample

runes.keystoneWhy: Taken on the 37.9%-win-rate, 38.7%-pick page — the movement-triggered heal and speed help you step in for Q stacks and then get back outside his 535-range Apprehend before it's up again.

summoners.why: Highest-winning combo in the data at 48.2% over the largest sample (41.4% pick) — Ghost lets you walk out of Apprehend range during his all-in windows, and Teleport keeps you resetting into a lane you're explicitly trying to prolong rather than end early.

playing.title: Farm every Q stack you can
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike (8/7/6/5/4s cooldown) permanently gets stronger on every kill. Every cooldown you let it sit idle on a lane you're down in is wasted long-term power.

playing.title: Respect the 535-range Apprehend
playing.detail: Don't stand inside his E range when it's up — once he hooks you in, the Q-auto-W bleed chain starts and a level 6 Noxian Guillotine can finish you outright for true damage.

playing.title: Wither to escape, not just to chase
playing.detail: W (Wither, 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown, 700 range) decelerates his movement and attack speed over time — use it the instant he commits to an all-in so you can walk away as the slow ramps up.

playing.title: Poke with Spirit Fire before committing
playing.detail: E (Spirit Fire, 12s cooldown, 650 range) reduces the armor of anyone standing in it — drop it under the minion wave before you trade so your autos and Q hit harder in the exchange.

playing.title: Disengage at high Hemorrhage stacks
playing.detail: If you're carrying four or five stacks of his passive, leave the fight. That's the enrage threshold where his attack damage spikes and his all-in becomes lethal.

playing.title: Survive to level 6, then trade harder
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands (120s cooldown, 400 range) gives bonus health and a health-drain aura for its duration — it's your first real tool to win an extended fight instead of just surviving one.

playing.title: Play the long game on purpose
playing.detail: The 48.5% win rate over 196 games means this lane is designed to be lost early and won late — don't force all-ins you don't need; stack Q, hit 18, and look to duel or split push once your stacks are maxed.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, boots, runes, summoners, and win rates above are pulled from measured Nasus-vs-Darius games on the current patch (16.20.1) — the tactical reading of why those numbers happen (Apprehend timing, Hemorrhage stacking, Q scaling) is my own analysis layered on top.

stats.opponentTip: Keep your distance from Darius’s Ghost and (E) ability. Focus on raising your [Q] stacks, and try to prolong the laning phase as much as possible.
